correctness.rationale: For any vertex excited at time t, b distinct causal predecessors at each earlier time form a collision-free embedded complete b-ary witness by refractory separation and tree acyclicity. Since the ambient complete b-ary height-h tree has exactly the witness vertex count, excitation at h must be at the global root (any other vertex has an original leaf more than h edges away) and force each height-j vertex excited at time j. This forces initial leaves 1, height-one vertices 0, and height-two vertices in {0,2}. Conversely, a local induction shows that if all b children are excited at time j-1, they cannot have been excited at j-2 or j-3, so the parent cannot be excited at j-2 or j-1 via at most its one external neighbor; it is 0 at j-1 and excited at j, with no restrictions on higher initial colors. The resulting independent choices produce the exact count and uniform probability. All edge heights 0, 1 and 2 are explicit. Direct C++17 enumeration covers 14,348,907 full binary height-three initial states and 1,594,323 ternary height-two states, as well as further conditioned cases; a second adversarial local-input checker validates 1,406,160 timing cases. The all-size conclusion is proof-based, not extrapolated.

originality.rationale: The general sharp extinction clock was already established. Bello and Sivakoff (2021), Lemma 4.7 and the probability product preceding Eq. (4.7), already provide the necessary three-layer conditions and corresponding finite-witness probability upper bound. The new result proves a nontrivial converse for the finite complete b-ary tree, including arbitrary parent feedback, showing that the existing upper bound is exactly attained and yielding a complete if-and-only-if extremizer classification and exact double-exponential terminal-shell probability. The converse and sharp finite-tree equality were not found in actual primary and published-record searches. The very close 2021 predecessor and inaccessible historical full texts are explicit novelty risks.

value.rationale: The exact population of states realizing a universal sharp extinction clock is a natural first-hitting-time tail, not an arbitrarily selected invariant. The causal-tree theorem shows the worst-case time but not how typical it is. The new forced-bottom-layer/free-interior characterization yields a surprising all-b exact fraction, and p(h+1)=p(h)^b quantifies a double-exponential separation of worst-case and typical trajectories. This is a complete unbounded-family classification with a structurally meaningful local-wave mechanism, independently of any broader theorem.
